title: Derived adjunctions under compatible changes of ring sheaves
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $T=U,V$, let $R_T,S_T$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $a_T:R_T\to S_T$ ring maps. Specify isomorphisms $c_R:u^{-1}R_V\xrightarrow{\sim}R_U$ and $c_S:u^{-1}S_V\xrightarrow{\sim}S_U$ satisfying $a_Uc_R=c_Su^{-1}a_V$. Write $D(R_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},R_T))$ and $D(S_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},S_T))$. Use these ordinary unbounded module derived categories and adjunctions $L_R=Lu_R^*\dashv R_R=Ru_{*,R}$ and $L_S=Lu_S^*\dashv R_S=Ru_{*,S}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $r_T:D(S_T)\to D(R_T)$ be termwise restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], which is exact. Then $r_T$ reflects isomorphisms, and there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$b:r_UL_S\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Rr_V,\qquad d:r_VR_S\xrightarrow{\sim}R_Rr_U.$$
The first comparison is induced by the identified-coefficient inverse image on module sheaves. The second is the derived direct-image comparison induced by the two equal composites of ringed-topos morphisms $(U,S_U)\to(V,R_V)$ through $(U,R_U)$ and through $(V,S_V)$. These comparisons respect the derived adjunctions in the following precise sense: for $M\in D(S_V)$, $N\in D(S_U)$ and $t:L_SM\to N$ with adjunct $t^\sharp:M\to R_SN$, the adjunct of $r_U(t)\circ b_M^{-1}:L_Rr_VM\to r_UN$ is $d_N\circ r_V(t^\sharp):r_VM\to R_Rr_UN$.

proof.text: Restriction leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged. The kernel and cokernel of a module-sheaf map have the same underlying abelian kernel and sheafified cokernel before and after restriction, so restriction is exact. The inverse of a bijective underlying sheaf map is linear for the larger ring: if $h$ is $S_T$-linear and bijective, then $h^{-1}(sx)=s h^{-1}(x)$ by applying $h$. Thus underived restriction reflects isomorphisms. On complexes $H^n(r_TK)=r_TH^n(K)$, because kernels and images are unchanged. This identification holds for derived morphisms by localization. If $r_T(f)$ is invertible, each $r_TH^n(f)$ is invertible; the preceding underived argument makes each $H^n(f)$ invertible, and the unbounded cohomology criterion makes $f$ invertible.

proof.text: Use the module inverse-image action construction in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Both $r_Uu_S^*M$ and $u_R^*r_VM$ have underlying abelian sheaf $u^{-1}M$. For $r\in R_U$ their actions agree: the first uses $c_S^{-1}a_U(r)$ in $u^{-1}S_V$, while the second uses $(u^{-1}a_V)c_R^{-1}(r)$; these are equal by $a_Uc_R=c_Su^{-1}a_V$. The identity of the underlying inverse-image sheaf is therefore a natural $R_U$-linear isomorphism. All four functors here are exact. Apply them termwise to complexes and descend this identity through localization, using clause (2) of the localization universal property. This gives the canonical $b:r_UL_S\cong L_Rr_V$ and its inverse, without any flatness assumption on $a_T$.

proof.text: Let $q_T:(T_{\mathrm{proet}},S_T)\to(T_{\mathrm{proet}},R_T)$ have underlying identity topos morphism and structural map $a_T$. Its module direct image is restriction of scalars. Exactness proved in step 1, together with the exact-functor derived-functor theorem, identifies $Rq_{T,*}$ with $r_T$ and identifies the derived comparison from underived restriction with the identity on termwise complexes. Let $p_R$ and $p_S$ denote the ringed-topos morphisms over $u$ given by $c_R,c_S$. Both $p_Rq_U$ and $q_Vp_S$ have underlying morphism $u$ and structural map $u^{-1}R_V\to S_U$; their two maps are $a_Uc_R$ and $c_Su^{-1}a_V$, equal by hypothesis. Hence they are the same morphism of ringed topoi.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; the two composites and exact vertical pushforwards

proof.text: Apply the general ringed-topos derived direct-image composition theorem to the two factorizations of the morphism in step 3. It identifies $r_VR_S$ and $R_Rr_U$ with the same total direct image, so their composite comparison gives the required canonical natural isomorphism $d$. More explicitly, represent $N$ by a complex, choose a K-injective resolution $q:N\to I$ over $S_U$, and choose a K-injective resolution $j:r_UI\to J$ over $R_U$. These exist on the small sites in the statement. The first route represents $r_VR_SN$ by $r_Vu_{*,S}I=u_{*,R}r_UI$, since $r_V$ is exact; the second represents $R_Rr_UN$ by $u_{*,R}J$, using the resolution $j r_Uq$. The normalization in the composition theorem says that $d_N$ is represented by $u_{*,R}j:u_{*,R}r_UI\to u_{*,R}J$ and that this is a quasi-isomorphism. No claim that $r_UI$ is K-injective is made.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; comparison on K-injective representatives

proof.text: For the specified $M,N,t$, choose complexes representing $M,N$ and resolutions $q,j$ as in step 4. Because $L_S$ is the exact termwise inverse image, and maps into $I$ are computed in the homotopy category, $t$ is represented by $Q(q)^{-1}Q(h)$ for a chain map $h:u_S^*M\to I$. The canonical derived adjunction formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], with the identity left-resolution and the chosen right-resolution, represents $t^\sharp$ by the underived adjunct $g:M\to u_{*,S}I$ of $h$. Under $b^{-1}$ the restricted map is represented by $j\,r_U(h):u_R^*r_VM\to J$. The underived adjunction in the operations definition uses the same abelian unit after forgetting the ring action, so the adjunct of $r_U(h)$ is $r_V(g):r_VM\to u_{*,R}r_UI$; the action calculation in step 2 supplies its $R_V$-linearity. Naturality of this adjunction makes the adjunct of $j\,r_U(h)$ equal to $(u_{*,R}j)\,r_V(g)$. Applying the same canonical derived-adjunction formula over $R$ shows that this chain map represents the adjunct of $r_U(t)b_M^{-1}$. By the explicit description of $d_N$ in step 4 it also represents $d_Nr_V(t^\sharp)$. Thus the two derived morphisms are equal. Changing chain representatives by homotopy does not change their classes, and the canonical resolution identifications cover arbitrary derived $M,N,t$.
